συνάγεσθαι καὶ μὴ σκορπίζειν, ἀλλ' ἐνδύεσθαι τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα ἀντιστῇ
πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου, ἀφ' ἑνὸς κελεύσματος εὐτάκτως
στρατοπεδεύουσα· ἔστι δὲ ἀβασίλευτος ὑπὸ τοῦ Φαραὼ, ἀλλ' οὐχ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ
τῶν Αἰγυπτίων οἱ πόνοι παραδίδονται ταύτῃ. Ἴσως δὲ διὰ μὴ βασιλεύεσθαι ἡμᾶς πρὸ
τῆς Χριστοῦ βασιλείας, ἀβασίλευτον ἡ ἀκρίς. Οὐ γὰρ ἔχουσιν ἡγούμενον, καθάπερ αἱ
μέλισσαι, ἀλλ' ἑκάστη ἡγεῖται. Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ προαιρέσει κουφιζόμενοι τῶν γηΐνων,
τεταγμένην ὁδεύοντες ζωήν. Ἢ καὶ ἀκρίδες, ὅσοι, τῇ νοήσει βουλόμενοι πέτεσθαι,
ἀδυνατοῦντες ὀλίγον τῆς γῆς ἀνατρέχουσιν. Εἰ δὲ πρακτικὸν μεταλάβοιεν, εἰς ἓν
τάγμα πρακτικὸν ἐναχθήσονται. Καὶ τράγος ἡγούμενος αἰπολίου. Τρίτος ὁ τράγος
κατὰ μόνους τοὺς Οʹ ἡγούμενος αἰπολίου, αὔξων τε καὶ πληθύνων αὐτὸ καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς
ἐν ὑψηλοῖς νομὰς ὁδηγῶν. Οὐδεμία γὰρ ἀγέλη ζώων οὕτως ἐπιβαίνει τῶν ὑψηλῶν.
Τοιοῦτος ὁ ἡγούμενος Χριστοῦ τοὺς ἐν τῷ αἰπο
pass_a_gloss: …and not scattering, but clothing herself with the full armor of God in order to stand against the methods of the devil, camping from one single order in good array; and she is without a king under Pharaoh, yet not under God, and the toils of the Egyptians are handed over to this one. Perhaps on account of our not being ruled as king before the kingship of Christ, the locust is without a king. For they do not have a leader, just as the bees do, but each one leads. These are the ones lightened by choice from the things of earth, traveling a life that has been set in order. Or also locusts are as many as, wanting to fly by thinking, being unable, run up a little from the earth. But if they should take a share of the practical, they will be led into one practical company. And a he-goat leading a herd of goats. Third is the he-goat according to the Seventy alone leading a herd of goats, both increasing and multiplying it and guiding it upon the pastures in high places. For no herd of living things so mounts upon the high places. Such is the one who leads those of Christ in the goat-herd, leading them up toward height. In another way the he-goat types Christ, being offered for sin. To this one who is in height there follows the whole multitude of those who revere God.
pass_b_english: …and not scattering, but putting on the full armor of God so as to stand against the devil’s schemes, camping in good order from one command. She is without a king under Pharaoh, but not under God, and the labors of the Egyptians are handed over to her. Perhaps because we were not under a king before Christ’s kingship, the locust is called kingless. They have no leader as bees do; each one leads. These are those lightened by choice from earthly things, walking an ordered life. Or locusts are also those who want to fly by intellect yet cannot, and so climb only a little from the earth. But if they share in the practical life, they will be led into one practical rank.

“And a he-goat leading a flock of goats.” Third is the he-goat—according to the Seventy alone—leading a goat flock, increasing and multiplying it and guiding it to pastures on the heights. No herd of animals climbs the high places like this. Such is the one who leads Christ’s people in the goat flock, raising them toward height. Otherwise the he-goat types Christ, offered for sin. To this one who is on high the whole multitude of the godly follows.

choices.choice: PG 13 Khazarzar; closes Prov 30 locust/he-goat stretch.
Kingless under Pharaoh vs ruled by God kept explicit.
Kept both pastoral-leader and sin-offering Christ typologies.
